cards.prose: Herod bound John for telling him the truth about his brother's wife, and the old story is the same. After Naboth's vineyard was taken, the word of Yahuah (the LORD) *came to Elijah the Tishbite* and sent him down to the king. John stands where Elijah stood, sent to a throne that had taken what was not its own.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sends Elijah to the king who has taken Naboth's vineyard, the same errand John carries to Herod.

cards.prose: Ahab runs to his wife with the report of what Elijah had done, and the queen answers with a threat on the prophet's life. In Herod's house John is bound *for Herodias’ sake*, so the one who rebukes the king is again met by a woman at the king's side.
cards.member_sentence: Ahab tells Jezebel and she threatens Elijah's life, as the woman behind Herod's throne turns on John.

cards.prose: Herod wanted John dead and held back because the crowd *counted him as a prophet*. The men answering Yahusha (Jesus) here hold back for the same reason, since *all hold John as a prophet*. The people knew what their rulers would not say out loud.
cards.member_sentence: The rulers questioned by Yahusha (Jesus) fear the people because all hold John as a prophet, as Herod did.

cards.prose: Herod hears the fame of Yahusha (Jesus) and takes him for John risen. Yahusha (Jesus) had already said who John was to those willing to hear it, *this is Elijah, which was for to come*. Herod's guess and the Master's word about John stand side by side.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says of John that this is Elijah who was for to come, the word set against Herod's guess.

cards.prose: John was done to as the rulers pleased, and Yahusha (Jesus) says so, *whatsoever they listed*. He then ties it to himself, *Likewise shall also the Son of Adam suffer of them*. What Herod did to John is the road ahead of the one Herod has just heard about.
cards.member_phrase: Elijah is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of Adam suffer of them.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says Elijah has come and was ill used, and that the Son of Adam will suffer the same from them.

cards.prose: Zechariah spoke because the Spirit of Elohim (God) came upon him, and what he said was a charge about the commandments of Yahuah (the LORD). The people he faced stoned him in the court. John spoke the same kind of word to Herod about what was lawful, and Herod's hearing of Yahusha (Jesus) comes from a house that has done this before.
cards.member_phrase: Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD), that ye cannot prosper?
cards.member_sentence: Zechariah the priest is moved by the Spirit to charge the people with breaking the commandments, and is put to death for it.

cards.prose: Herod hears of Yahusha (Jesus) with John's blood fresh in his house. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the teachers before him that the sending of prophets goes on and that *some of them ye shall kill and crucify*. John was one killed, and he says plainly that more are coming.
cards.member_phrase: some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says he sends prophets and wise men and some will be killed, scourged and driven from city to city.

cards.prose: John finished what he was sent to say to Herod and was killed for it. In Revelation the witnesses are overcome *when they shall have finished their testimony*, and again the ones who speak the word to the end are the ones put to death. Herod's act is not the last of its kind.
cards.member_phrase: when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them
cards.member_sentence: The witnesses are killed when they have finished their testimony, a likeness to John's end at Herod's hand.
cards.flag: Old note read the two witnesses as the Elijah pattern's second fulfilment at the second coming; I kept only the plain likeness (testimony finished, then killed) since the witnesses are set after the reign, not before the Day.

cards.prose: Matthew tells why John was bound, and Mark tells what it did to Herod. When the fame of Yahusha (Jesus) reached him, he said that John *was risen from the dead*. A king who jailed the prophet for a woman's sake could not hear of power without thinking of the man he had silenced.
cards.member_phrase: he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him
cards.member_sentence: Mark gives Herod's conflicted reaction: he says John is risen from the dead and so these works show forth in him.

cards.prose: When Yahusha (Jesus) goes out to a desert place and the people follow on foot, they are in a wilderness where bread was given before. In Exodus it lay *upon the face of the wilderness* after the dew went up, a gift from Yahuah (the LORD) to people who had nothing to eat in that place.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) gives the manna on the face of the wilderness, the bread of the desert that this crowd now stands in.

cards.prose: A people with nothing to eat in a desert is not new. The manna that kept Yashar'el (Israel) alive *was as coriander seed*, plain food given day after day by Yahuah (the LORD). Here a crowd follows Yahusha (Jesus) out of the cities into a desert place and he feeds them.
cards.member_sentence: The manna described as coriander seed is the plain wilderness bread that kept Yashar'el (Israel) alive.

cards.prose: Elisha was handed twenty barley loaves and told, *Give unto the people, that they may eat*, and the bread proved more than it looked. Yahusha (Jesus) is handed five loaves and two fishes in a desert place and feeds a far larger crowd, so the greater prophet stands where the lesser once stood.
cards.member_phrase: brought the man of Elohim (God) bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley
cards.member_sentence: A man brings twenty barley loaves to Elisha, who orders them given to the people, the first small feeding in a desert land.

cards.prose: Isaiah names a day when Yahuah (the LORD) makes *a feast of fat things* on his mountain. Here the hungry sit down on the grass in a desert place and eat until they are filled, and the table in the wilderness shows the kind of host Isaiah was speaking of.
cards.member_phrase: shall Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) make unto all people a feast of fat things
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) will spread a feast on his mountain, a larger table than the one in the wilderness.

cards.prose: The same hands do the same acts in both. He *took* the bread, *blessed* it, *brake* it and gave it to the disciples, on the grass with a great crowd and then at the table with the twelve. The disciples are the ones who carry what he breaks out to the people.
cards.member_phrase: took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples
cards.member_sentence: At the last supper he takes, blesses, breaks and gives bread to the disciples, as he did before the five thousand.

cards.prose: Twelve baskets of fragments are taken up once the crowd is filled, and later he tells his followers they will sit upon *twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)*. The number is the number of the tribes, and the flock he feeds in the desert is the flock those tribes make up.
cards.member_phrase: ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) promises twelve thrones for those who followed him, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.prose: John sets the same crossing to a desert place beside a feast, *And the passover, a feast of the Yahudim (Jews), was nigh.* (John 6:4) The bread in the wilderness is given in the season when Yashar'el (Israel) remembers being brought out of Egypt.
cards.member_sentence: John says the same crossing came when the Passover was near, so the wilderness bread falls in the season of the exodus.

cards.prose: John records the crowd themselves tying the bread to the old gift, *Our fathers did eat manna in the desert*. Matthew's desert place and the feeding fit those words, because the people knew whose bread this recalled.
cards.member_sentence: The crowd says their fathers ate manna in the desert, naming the old bread the feeding recalls.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) sees the great multitude and is *moved with compassion toward them*, and heals their sick. Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) says in Ezekiel that he will *search my sheep, and seek them out*, and here the shepherd has gone out to them himself.
cards.member_sentence: Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) promises to search for his own sheep and seek them out, the work the shepherd does here.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) goes out to a desert place and the crowd follows, and later he says *I have compassion on the multitude* and will not send them away fasting. The shepherd feeds a crowd in the wilderness twice, and the second time his own words give the reason.
cards.member_phrase: I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat
cards.member_sentence: He says he has compassion on the crowd and will not send them away hungry, the second feeding in the wilderness.

cards.prose: Habakkuk says to Yahuah (the LORD), *Thou didst walk through the sea*, and in the fourth watch Yahusha (Jesus) is walking on it. The one the prophet spoke of as walking the waters is the one the disciples see coming toward them in the flesh.
cards.member_sentence: Habakkuk says Yahuah (the LORD) walked through the sea, the same walk the disciples see on the water.

cards.prose: *It is I* is his answer to the frightened men in the boat. In John he says *Before Abraham was, I am*. The one who spoke with Abraham is the one speaking across the water, the Word who walked with the fathers and has come in the flesh.
cards.member_sentence: He says that before Abraham was, I am, the self-naming that sounds in it is I on the sea.

cards.prose: John carries the very words Matthew has, spoken to men afraid of what they saw on the water, *It is I; be not afraid*. They had cried out that it was a spirit, and what met their fear was not an argument but his voice telling them who was there.
cards.member_sentence: John tells the same scene with the same words, it is I, be not afraid.

cards.prose: In the boat they worshipped and said *thou art the Son of Elohim (God)*. Later Peter, asked, says *the Son of the living Elohim (God)*, and adds that he is the Messiah (Christ). The boat said it in awe, and Peter says it plainly.
cards.member_sentence: Peter confesses him as the Messiah (Christ), the Son of the living Elohim (God), the same word the boat spoke.

cards.prose: At the first storm the disciples go into a ship because they *followed him*, with the Master aboard. Here he constrains them to go before him and stays on the mountain while the wind is against them. In both boats they learn who it is they follow, and here the end of it is worship.
cards.member_sentence: He enters a ship, his disciples follow, and a storm rises, the first boat before the walking on the sea.

cards.prose: Herod says *This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead*, and the disciples later report that the people say the same, *Some say that thou art John the Baptist*. Herod's guess was the street's guess. They name John, Elijah or a prophet, and not the one in front of them.
cards.member_sentence: The crowds guess John, Elijah or a prophet, the same kind of guess Herod made about him.

cards.prose: Herod says the same thing in both tellings, that John is risen from the dead, and Mark adds the words that give him away, *whom I beheaded*. He does not speak as a man who thinks the matter is closed.
cards.member_sentence: Mark gives Herod saying it is John whom he beheaded, risen from the dead.

cards.prose: Herod had taken *his brother Philip’s wife*, and the commandment names exactly that, *thy brother’s wife*. When John told him it was not lawful he was not giving an opinion, he was reading Herod what Yahuah (the LORD) had given through Moses.
cards.member_sentence: The commandment forbids uncovering a brother's wife, the law John stood on against Herod.

cards.prose: The second place the Torah speaks of it carries the penalty, that such a man *hath uncovered his brother’s nakedness*, and *they shall be childless*. Herod's marriage to Philip's wife is a thing the commandment calls unclean, and John would call it nothing else.
cards.member_sentence: Taking a brother's wife is called an unclean thing with childlessness as its penalty, the law behind John's rebuke.

cards.prose: Ahab sulks over a vineyard he cannot have, and his wife comes in to ask what is wrong, and then takes the matter into her own hands and writes the letters herself. In Herod's house John is bound *for Herodias’ sake*, and the king's own woman is the one who pushes the matter on.
cards.member_sentence: Jezebel comes to Ahab and takes the matter into her own hands, as Herodias does with Herod.

cards.prose: Twice in one chapter he goes apart. When John is dead he goes by ship into *a desert place apart*, and when the crowds have been fed and sent away he climbs the mountain *apart to pray* and is *there alone*.
cards.member_phrase: he went up into a mountain apart to pray: and when the evening was come, he was there alone
cards.member_sentence: After sending the crowds away he goes up the mountain alone to pray as evening comes.

cards.prose: Matthew says only that he went to a desert place apart. Mark gives his words to the disciples, *Come ye yourselves apart*, because they had no leisure even to eat. The withdrawing was for their sake too.
cards.member_phrase: Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while
cards.member_sentence: Mark records his invitation to the disciples to come apart into a desert place and rest.

cards.prose: The same acts come again at Emmaus. At the table he *took bread, and blessed it, and brake*, and gave to them, and in Luke it is then that their eyes are opened and they know him. What the five thousand saw done on the grass, those two see done at a table.
cards.member_sentence: At Emmaus he takes, blesses, breaks and gives bread, and the two travellers know him.

cards.prose: Twelve baskets are taken up after the crowd is filled, and the wall of the city stands on *twelve foundations* with the names of the twelve apostles. The twelve who carried the bread to the people are the twelve whose names are set in the wall, beside the gates with the names of the tribes.
cards.member_phrase: twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb
cards.member_sentence: The wall of the city has twelve foundations carrying the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

cards.prose: Here he goes up *into a mountain* alone to pray. At the opening of the Sermon he climbs one too, with the disciples coming to him to hear. The mountain is where he prays to the Father and where he teaches the Father's commandments.
cards.member_sentence: Seeing the crowds he goes up a mountain and the disciples come to him, the mountain of the Sermon.

cards.prose: He goes up *into a mountain apart* to pray with no one, and later he takes three of the disciples up an high mountain apart, where Moses and Elijah appear talking with him. In both he leaves the crowd behind to be with the Father.
cards.member_sentence: He takes Peter, James and John up an high mountain apart, where Moses and Elijah appear with him.

cards.prose: Alone on the mountain he prays until evening, and at Gethsemane he leaves the disciples sitting and goes to *pray yonder*. On the night he is taken he does what he did here, he withdraws from the ones with him to pray to the Father.
cards.member_sentence: At Gethsemane he tells the disciples to sit here while he goes to pray.

cards.prose: The mountain where he prayed alone comes back at the close of the book as the mountain *where Yahusha (Jesus) had appointed them*. What he began apart at evening he finishes by gathering the eleven there.
cards.member_sentence: The eleven go into Galilee to the mountain where he had appointed them.

cards.prose: *Be not afraid* in the boat is what Elohim (God) says to his own people in Isaiah, *Fear thou not; for I am with thee*. He gives the reason before the command, and the reason is who is speaking, *I am thy Elohim (God)*.
cards.member_phrase: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) tells Yashar'el (Israel) to fear not because he is with them and is their Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Isaiah gives the same comfort with a hand attached, *will hold thy right hand*, saying *Fear not*, and promising help. In the boat the words come over the water first, and the hand comes after.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says he will hold thy right hand and help, saying fear not.

cards.prose: In the boat they say *thou art the Son of Elohim (God)*, and in the psalm Yahuah (the LORD) says it first, *Thou art my Son*. What the men on the water spoke had already been declared.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) declares thou art my Son, the word the men in the boat speak.

cards.prose: The woman with the issue of blood came behind him and touched *the hem of his garment*, and here the whole country asks to *only touch the hem of his garment*. What one woman reached for in secret, the region now asks for in the open.
cards.member_phrase: came behind him, and touched the hem of his garment
cards.member_sentence: A woman diseased twelve years touches the hem of his garment from behind, the same touch the country seeks.

cards.prose: The psalm that speaks of a way through the sea goes on, *Thou leddest thy people like a flock*, by the hand of Moses and Aaron. In the fourth watch Yahusha (Jesus) comes to his own over the water, the shepherd crossing the sea he once led them through.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) led his people like a flock through the sea by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

new_threads.title: The mountain where he goes apart to pray
new_threads.summary_md:
The chapter shows Yahusha (Jesus) going apart twice. When he heard that John was dead, he left by ship for a lonely place, and then, after the crowds had been fed and sent away, he went up a mountain by himself.

*When Yahusha (Jesus) heard of it, he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard thereof, they followed him on foot out of the cities.* (Matthew 14:13)

*And when he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into a mountain apart to pray: and when the evening was come, he was there alone.* (Matthew 14:23)

Those two verses hold the same movement, the withdrawing to the Father after a death and after a crowd, and the mountains elsewhere in Matthew carry the same marks. At the opening of the Sermon the multitudes bring him up the hill and the disciples come to him there.

*And seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain: and when he was set, his disciples came unto him:* (Matthew 5:1)

Later he takes three of them away, and Moses and Elijah talk with him.

*And after six days Yahusha (Jesus) taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart,* (Matthew 17:1)

On the night he is taken he leaves the disciples sitting and goes by himself to pray.

*Then cometh Yahusha (Jesus) with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder.* (Matthew 26:36)

And at the end of the book the eleven are sent to a mountain he chose for them.

*Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Yahusha (Jesus) had appointed them.* (Matthew 28:16)

Each of these is a place where he is apart from the crowd and with the Father, whether he is praying alone, teaching his disciples, standing with Moses and Elijah, or sending out the eleven. The mountain in Matthew 14 is the first of these where he is wholly alone, and it comes straight after the feeding in the wilderness.
